 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Seattle Seahawks seemed every bit as dominant as last season when they started 2-0. Since then, though, they've lost three of their last four games and are coming into a Week 7 game against the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs on a two-game losing streak.
 However, things went from bad to worse this week. The hope was that Zach Charbonnet would be making his long-awaited return for the franchise. But his comeback has been delayed for at least one more week.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement What Happened to Zach Charbonnet?
 Last year, the Seahawks made great use of Charbonnet and Kenneth Walker III in the running game. But a torn ACL in the Divisional Round ended the season early for the former, while the latter went on to win Super Bowl MVP.
 Charbonnet began the season on the physically unable to perform list and returned to practice on October 1. Seattle officially activated him to its 53-man roster on October 22 after he participated fully in preparations for the Chiefs game. However, Macdonald decided to delay his season debut.
 When Will Charbonnet Return?
 For the time being, the expectation is that Charbonnet will be back on the field at any moment. Macdonald explained that he wanted him to finish the ramping-up process before seeing NFL action.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "We're going along with the plan. The plan was to get a great week's worth of work and see where we're at, so we're going to take it into next week. I would just say it's part of the plan. Zach's doing great, and we'll go into next week and see how it goes."
 SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN's Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer 
 He did clarify that there weren't any setbacks in the recovery process, and he confirmed that it was "going as good as we could have hoped."
 Charbonnet's next opportunity to make his season debut will come against the Chicago Bears on November 2.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Seahawks' Outlook Without Charbonnet
 A second-round pick in 2023, Charbonnet came into his own last season when he tallied 730 yards and 12 touchdowns, ranking at number 18 in PFN's Running Back Impact Metric . His absence, coupled with Walker being on the Chiefs, has severely impacted the Seahawks.
 Their lead rusher, Emmanuel Wilson, is at 303 rushing yards with an average of 3.5 yards per carry. As a result, they don't have a single running back in the top-40 in the RBi rankings.
 Seattle's inconsistent rushing attack has added to the offense's challenges. Meanwhile, Sam Darnold has thrown seven interceptions in 2026, highlighting another area the Seahawks must improve as they attempt to end their losing streak.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In four full games, Darnold has already thrown seven interceptions with no run game to fall back on. They'll be hoping for a turnaround against the Chiefs from the offense as a whole, but at the very least, help is on the way sooner rather than later.
